newsitem.title: USA: Marcum sells unit to Natural Fuels Corp.
newsitem.headline: Marcum sells unit to Natural Fuels Corp.

text.p: Marcum Natural Gas Services Inc on Tuesday said it agreed to sell substantially all of the assets of its wholly-owned subsidiary Marcum Fuel Systems Inc to Natural Fuels Corp, which is an affiliate of both Public Service Co of Colorado and Coastal Corp's Colorado Interstate Gas Co.
The disposition of all assets is expected to result in net cash proceeds of about $1 million, a portion of which will come from the sale to Natural Fuels, Marcum said.

Marcum said it also expects to receive additional cash proceeds during the next 12 months from a shared interest in the gross margins related to pending projects awarded to Marcum Fuel Systems or Natural Fuels that were based upon quotes issued by Marcum Fuel Systems.

In addition, Marcum Natural Gas Services will receive a royalty on future sales of its proprietary sonic nozzle dispensing equipment that could enhance cash proceeds from the sale over the next five to ten years.
Marcum said it expects a charge of $1.3 million against the carrying value of Marcum Fuel Systems will be recognized by the company in the first quarter of 1997.
Due to the proposed sale, Marcum Natural Gas Services will restate its 1996 and 1995 results of operations to account for the Marcum Fuel Systems operations as discontinued operations.
Natural Fuels will be purchasing the inventory and property of Marcum Fuel Systems and assuming responsibility for completion of all projects in backlog. rain in Europe.
CORN - Down 1-1/2 to one cent a bushel- Led by new crop on USDA weekly planting progress figure of 50 percent. Ideas that USDA numbers understated planting pace, traders said.

SOYBEANS - Three cents a bushel lower to unchanged - Old crop months supported by tight stocks situation and talk of error in deliveries while weakness in new crop contracts on ideas that soybean planting progress off to a good start.
SOY PRODUCTS - Soymeal up $0.30 to down $0.30 per ton, and soyoil up 0.12 to 0.01 cent per lb higher.
